Nothing narrowed.
  > 
  > 1. **P5 (a–c).** (a) S is now the deviation of the other specs from the pre-chosen reporting spec, and the within-cell Spearman is read as the excess over a correct-spec noise-only null simulation (same for the bootstrap SE and the benchmarks); if the mechanical part is large S is replaced by a variant excluding the reporting spec. (b) L is tested across cells/graph draws against realised variance, not within a cell; the within-cell test is on the centred error and only for S and the bootstrap SE. (c) Part (i) is tested on realised variance, part (ii) on |realised bias| (S computed on one random half of the draws, bias on the other), with the combined leave-one-mechanism/family-out R² on top. CI resamples at mechanism/family level; per-held-out-group gains are reported; the rule now has three outcomes (supported: gain ≥0.05 with group-level CI excluding 0, positive in ≥4 of 6 mechanisms, survives dropping any one group; inconclusive: point gain but CI includes 0; not supported). Low power with 6 groups is stated.
  > 2. **Cell budget.** Written into the Brief as a proposal (≈160 cells: 54 core + 9 s=0 nulls, one per (d, p) + slices for p grid, s, σ, cluster designs, families, real graphs, edge noise); Tier G ≈3×10⁴ replicates; Tier A on ≈30 cells with ≈100 draws. The analysis role confirms or cuts; the rest is exploratory.
  > 3. **Edge noise** is back as a slice (mechanisms a and e, q ∈ {10%, 30%}); P5 is also tested there.
  > 4. DM bias = s·τ under Bernoulli only, measured per cell under cluster designs; held-out-corner check defined (fit below the 0.7 exposure quantile, score above, added to the CV loss); one labelled cross-tier summary figure; SNR tabulated per mechanism × s.
